name: Robusta coffee (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Robusta coffee (Coffea canephora) [Coffee and coffee products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: Wang et al. 2019, Coffea robusta cultivars, Hainan - fatty acids, amino acids, protein, lipid (PMC6332462)
Selected metals in coffee, atomic absorption - minerals (PMC6778417)
Yeretzian et al., Acids in coffee: review & meta-analysis, Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr, doi:10.1080/10408398.2021.1957767
Botanical & Geographical Characterization of Green Coffee, J Agric Food Chem, doi:10.1021/jf8037117 - caffeine, chlorogenic acids
Organic Compounds in Green Coffee Beans (ResearchGate 282595074)
Illy & Viani, Espresso Coffee: The Science of Quality - green-coffee proximate composition
US patent US4976983 - green Robusta malic acid range
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources for microbial growth on green Robusta: the chlorogenic-acid pool (~8 g/100g, hydrolyzable to quinic + caffeic acid), sucrose (~4 g/100g), and cell-wall galactomannan/arabinogalactan (~43 g/100g, requires mannan/galactan-degrading enzymes). Free glucose/fructose are minor (~0.3 g each). Nitrogen comes from protein/amino acids (~13 g/100g, Glu/Asp-rich) plus the alkaloids caffeine (~2.2%) and trigonelline (~0.7%). Robusta is defined by high caffeine and chlorogenic a
curation_added: chlorogenic acids (total, ~8 g/100g) - the single largest organic-acid pool, absent from current profile
caffeine amount (~2.2 g/100g) - was only in uncovered names, now quantified
citric acid, quinic acid, malic acid, acetic acid - organic acids, all absent
specific free sugars with amounts (sucrose, glucose, fructose) and bound galactomannan/arabinogalactan
full quantified amino-acid profile (16 amino acids)
quantified fatty-acid profile (6 fatty acids) and total oil
quantified mineral amounts (K, Mg, Ca, Fe, Cu, Zn, Na, Ni, P, Mn) - K is dominant

curation_removed.name: Cholesterol
curation_removed.reason: Animal sterol, biologically implausible in a plant seed. Coffee lipids carry the diterpenes cafestol/kahweol and plant sterols (sitosterol/stigmasterol), not cholesterol. FooDB predicted/mis-assigned.

curation_removed.name: Cyanocobalamin
curation_removed.reason: Vitamin B12 is absent from plant foods (no plant B12 biosynthesis); FooDB predicted, not measured.

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: Preformed vitamin A (retinol) does not occur in plants; the real provitamin form is beta-carotene, which is retained. FooDB artifact.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+)
curation_removed.reason: Duplicate iron entry; consolidated into a single 'iron' component.

curation_removed.name: Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: Subcellular-compartment artifact (a BiGG/FooDB compartment tag), not a distinct food nutrient; consolidated into 'iron'.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Free cobalt ion; non-nutritive trace with no defined role in coffee except via B12 (which is absent). Not a growth nutrient of this food.

curation_removed.name: Starch C12H20O10
curation_removed.reason: Green coffee beans contain essentially no starch; their storage polysaccharides are galactomannan and type-II arabinogalactan (now represented explicitly). FooDB mis-assignment.

curation_removed.name: Iodine c
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive trace/contaminant element; not a defining nutrient of coffee.

curation_removed.name: Fluoride
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive trace/contaminant element; not a growth nutrient of the bean.

curation_removed.name: D-Serine
curation_removed.reason: D-enantiomer artifact; the proteinogenic form present in coffee protein is L-serine (included in the amino-acid list).

curation_removed.name: Chromium
curation_removed.reason: Trace/contaminant element, not quantified and not a defining coffee nutrient; drop as noise (borderline; harmless if kept).

oxygen_note: food substrate; O2 availability is a simulation condition, not a property of the food
basis: per 100 g green (raw) coffee beans, Coffea canephora var. Robusta, dry-weight basis. NOTE: FooDB FOOD00060 is the coffee bean; roasting destroys most sucrose/free sugars and part of the chlorogenic acids and trigonelline (generating quinic/caffeic acid, niacin, melanoidins), and brewing extracts only the water-soluble fraction. Values below are for the GREEN bean, the best-characterized and least-transformed form.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
